## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators recovering a failed session SQLite migration could see a broken emoji or replacement character in the generated sanitized failure report or its prefilled GitHub issue link when text crossed a report length boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor-owned failure-report builder uses the shared UTF-16-safe prefix helper at its existing 500-character field, 20,000-character issue-body, and 6,000-character URL-body limits. Redaction rules, report schema, CLI flags, file formats, URLs, and maximum lengths are unchanged.

The branch has also been rebased across the current migration-manifest hardening: the resolution preserves main's Zod parsing and path-safety behavior while retaining only the Unicode-safe truncation change. The regression fixture now uses a schema-valid non-empty agent ID.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content. It also normalizes already-persisted short-term recall entries and regenerates their concept tags.

Closes #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or weakening retrieval quality.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- The existing short-term repair command cleans stored envelopes, remains idempotent, and recalculates derived concept tags.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before

```text
11: @@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)
12: first remembered line
13:
14: 12: legitimate numbered prose
```

### After

```text
first remembered line

12: legitimate numbered prose
```

Structured location remains `startLine: 10`, `endLine: 13`.

### Validation

Validated after rebasing onto current `origin/main` with safe Node 24.18.0:

- `qmd-snippet.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `short-term-promotion.test.ts`: 72/72 passed.
- Focused QMD integration selection: 11/11 passed, including both single-endpoint line-range branches.
- Strict standalone TypeScript check for the new parser: passed.
- Changed files: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent post-implementation review: approved with no unaddressed findings.

A full extensions type-check on current main also reports unrelated dependency/type failures outside this patch. It initially caught strict capture-index errors in the new parser; those were fixed, and the parser now passes an isolated strict TypeScript check.

The repository autoreview launcher could not invoke a shell review engine in this OpenClaw-native Codex environment, so an independent native Codex review was run against the actual diff instead.

Remote Crabbox validation was attempted but unavailable in this environment: the configured Blacksmith provider has no `blacksmith` executable, and the AWS fallback has no usable credentials. No untrusted patch was run outside the repository checkout.

## AI Assistance

This patch was implemented with Codex assistance. The behavior was independently audited before and after implementation, and all reported findings were verified against source and tests.

Maintainers may edit this branch.

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Production-path connect-timeout storm proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The storm case runs production `openStream` → `urbitFetch` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against a real loopback `node:http` server that returns `503` five times; real timers; each armed `setTimeout(..., 60000)` is cleared. The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers, including under repeated failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` + closed-port TCP failure; production SSRF-guarded transport (no `urbitFetch` mock, no fake timers).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Same `try/finally { clearTimeout }` pattern as `extensions/zalouser/src/probe.ts`; no new config/API.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners and real timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.90s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Five sequential non-OK connects each arm then clear a 60s connect timer with matching `clearTimeout(handle)`; a real transport reject also clears its single connect timer.
- **What was not tested:** Live Urbit ship reconnect storm against a real Tlon host; SSE stream body processing after a successful connect.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Successful connects still clear the timer after headers; only failed connects gain the missing cleanup.

target.title: fix(clawhub): reject calendar-invalid feed timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed ClawHub promotions feed with an impossible calendar date (e.g. `2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z`) would be accepted because `Date.parse` silently normalizes it. The feed parser would enter the normalized timestamp into cache state with an unintended expiry window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` — the same calendar validator adopted by the recent commitments fix (#106236) — to reject ISO timestamps whose calendar components are not real dates before they enter cache state. Both `generatedAt` and `expiresAt` are validated; canonical leap-day and normal ISO dates continue to parse without change.

## User Impact

Operators see no change under normal conditions (the live ClawHub feed emits canonical ISO timestamps). If a remote feed snapshot is ever malformed with an impossible date, it is now rejected with a clear error instead of silently acquiring the wrong cache-expiry window.

## Evidence

**Before** (`upstream/main` cae29a07920): `parseClawHubPromotionsFeed` accepted `generatedAt: "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z"` and returned the feed unchanged — the impossible date entered cache state.

**Premise**: `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` validates the ISO calendar shape and rejects impossible dates via `setUTCFullYear` round-trip checks; this is the same validator used by `src/commitments/extraction.ts` and `src/cron/parse.ts`. The ClawHub feed parser has no other timestamp validation before the `Date.parse` call.

**After** (`fix/clawhub-calendar-valid-feed-timestamps`):
```
PASS: canonical valid — parsed OK
PASS: generatedAt Feb 30 — rejected: Malformed ClawHub promotions feed: timestamps must be ISO dates.
PASS: expiresAt Feb 30 — rejected: Malformed ClawHub promotions feed: timestamps must be ISO dates.
PASS: leap day 2028-02-29 — parsed OK
PASS: not-a-date — rejected: Malformed ClawHub promotions feed: timestamps must be ISO dates.
PASS: non-ISO string — rejected: Malformed ClawHub promotions feed: timestamps must be ISO dates.
```

**Focused tests**: `src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` — 19 passed (2 new: calendar-invalid rejection + leap-day acceptance).

**What was not tested**: The live ClawHub endpoint currently emits canonical `Date.toISOString()` values, so the reject path is not exercised in production. Full CI will exercise the broader test matrix.

target.title: fix(codex): stop warning when a non-Codex-native run has no mirrored history
target.body:
> Resubmit of #106912, which was auto-closed by the active-PR-limit bot. Same tested commit; unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server harness also runs non-OpenAI models (Claude/Haiku). On those runs — and on the first turn of any new session — there is no Codex-native mirrored session transcript to read, which is expected. `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages()` nonetheless emitted a `warn` ("failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks") on every such turn, and channels render that `agent/embedded` warn as `⚠️ 🧰 Process: <name> failed`, so operators see a routine, non-fatal condition as an error. (Reported in #106556.)

## Why This Change Was Made

`readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages()` already distinguishes the cases: a missing file (ENOENT) returns `[]`, and a present-but-not-Codex-native mirror returns `undefined`. Every caller tolerates the miss and falls back to existing history (`?? []`, `?? historyState.messages`), so the `undefined` return is expected control flow, not a failure. The wrapper's warning also carried no error cause (only `sessionFile`), so it was low signal. This change downgrades it from `warn` to `debug` with clearer wording — the minimal, behavior-preserving fix (no control-flow or return-contract change) for a path under the Codex extension gate. The `undefined` return stays load-bearing for the two call sites that fall back to prior history.

Note: this is a log-severity change on OpenClaw's own mirrored-session reader (OpenClaw session-entry format), not Codex wire-protocol or runtime behavior.

## User Impact

Non-Codex-native and first-turn runs routed through the Codex harness no longer surface a spurious failed "Process" to operators. Genuine failures were already swallowed upstream and are unaffected; the run still completes via the existing fallback.

## Evidence

- New regression in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`: a mirror whose first entry is not a `session` header returns `undefined`, emits **no** `warn`, and logs `debug` instead. Full file green (6 passed) via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`. The prior "missing history → [] without warn" test still passes.
- `git diff --check` clean; 2 files, +35/−1; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit.
- Source-reproducible: the noise is a fixed `warn` on an expected `undefined` return; a live Codex run is not needed to demonstrate it.

Fixes #106556

target.title: fix: tighten findSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer with execution guard
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `findSchema.limit` accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Max results" is inherently an integer-valued field. Float values like `limit=5.5` silently pass `Type.Number` validation and reach tool execution with ambiguous behavior.

**Solution**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer()` with a runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` execution guard. **Per ClawSweeper review, `minimum: 1` has been removed** — zero and negative values retain the existing runtime normalization behavior, so the change only rejects fractional (non-integer) values.

**What changed / NOT changed**:
1. Schema: `Type.Number()` → `Type.Integer()` (no minimum constraint)
2. Runtime: `Number.isSafeInteger(limit)` guard rejects non-integer at execution boundary
3. Focused regression tests (10 cases): valid int, float rejection, zero/negative acceptance (preserved normalization), optional, required pattern, execution boundary
4. Root proof script removed per ClawSweeper review

The runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` guard rejects fractional values at the tool-call boundary. `normalizePositiveLimit` handles value clamping. Zero and negative values continue to be normalized at runtime (existing behavior preserved).

**merge-risk declaration**: Low — schema + guard change to internal tool parameter. Only fractional values are rejected; zero and negative values retain existing runtime normalization. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved.

target.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP calls only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Gateway `/v1/embeddings` and capability-CLI paths call `embed` / `embedBatch` without a signal, so a server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers could hang the request forever. Memory/wiki callers already install their own deadlines; this gap is the unsignaled transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `signal` is omitted, install operation-specific hang bounds via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`:

- `embed` (query): 60s — aligned with memory remote query defaults
- `embedBatch` (batch): 120s — aligned with memory remote batch defaults so gateway/CLI batches are not clamped below established batch policy

When a caller already provides a signal, leave that deadline alone so memory search / tool timeouts are not clamped.

No new config surface. Test-only override shortens the floor for hang repros.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding requests (gateway HTTP embeddings, capability CLI) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Unsignaled query requests fail after 60s; unsignaled batch requests fail after 120s (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`). Callers that pass `AbortSignal` keep their own budget.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (`postEmbeddingRequest`, query/batch floors)
- Production caller under test: `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider(...).provider.embed` / `embedBatch` against a real local `node:http` server that never responds
- Regression: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- Sibling cases still green in the same file (UTF-16 error bounds, oversized JSON cancel, auth/config paths)

### Unit regression


```text
 ✓ |plugins| ... > keeps caller AbortSignal deadlines instead of the no-signal transport floor 205ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 27.79s
```

### Standalone runtime proof (outside Vitest)

```bash
# against real hung node:http (accepts body, never writes response)
EOF
```

```text
{"proof":"standalone-production-provider-embedBatch-no-signal","path":"createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider().provider.embedBatch","callerShape":"gateway embeddings-http / capability CLI (unsignaled)","upstream":"real node:http accepts body, never writes response","batchResult":{"ok":false,"error":{"name":"TimeoutError","message":"request timed out"}},"batchElapsedMs":207,"expectedFloorMs":180,"rejectedBeforeHangCap":true}

{"proof":"standalone-caller-AbortSignal-not-clamped","signaled":{"type":"still-pending"}}
standalone-proof: done
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding POSTs no longer hang forever when the upstream accepts the connection but never responds; query and batch use distinct floors (60s / 120s).
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway `embeddings-http` / capability CLI / direct provider → `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider` → `embed` (query) or `embedBatch` (batch) → `postEmbeddingRequest` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` when `signal` is absent.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`. Query/batch floors match memory-core remote budgets (`60_000` / `120_000`). Does not override caller-owned signals used by memory-core `runEmbeddingOperationWithTimeout`. Does not add config/env.

target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Anthropic-style HTTP 400 error responses arrive as raw JSON bodies with no leading HTTP status prefix. The failover classifier cannot infer the HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` and returns `null`, so the configured model fallback chain is never consulted — users see a terminal error despite healthy fallback models being available.

**Solution**: Added a check in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` that detects `invalid_request_error` from the structured API error type via the existing `parseApiErrorInfo` helper and classifies it as `"format"`, which triggers the model fallback chain. The check is placed after auth/billing/rate-limit/context-overflow classifiers so more specific reasons take precedence. `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` is checked before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to ensure model-unavailable semantics are preserved when the payload indicates a model-not-found condition (#101414 review fix).

Also fixed `isSchemaErrorMessage()` to exclude structured `invalid_request_error` payloads. Without this exclusion, `isSchemaErrorMessage` would match via `classifyFailoverReason(raw) === "format"` and `classifyProviderRuntimeFailureKind` would incorrectly return `"schema"` instead of `"format"`, defeating the primary fix's effect in the runtime-failure path.

**What changed**: 7 files, ~+182/-4 lines — one classifier rule addition in `errors.ts` (line 1146), reordered `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` to preserve model_not_found precedence (review fix #101414), one early-exit guard in `isSchemaErrorMessage()` (line 599) to prevent schema/format collision, one whitelist entry in `result-fallback-classifier.ts` (belt-and-suspenders), a `runWithModelFallback` integration test in `model-fallback.test.ts` to exercise the actual fallback machinery, a `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` regression, a `failover-error.test.ts` cover, and a formatter-sync test in `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`. Total: 14 new test cases across 5 test files (+1 updated for model_not_found precedence).

**What NOT changed**: No provider connections, no credentials, no configuration schema, no public API signatures, no lockfile or changelog.

Fixes #99174

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" (instead of null) for Anthropic invalid_request_error JSON bodies.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v25.9.0, OpenClaw main @ ae397906aa
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx docs/.local/issue-99174-evidence.ts` against actual exported classifiers with realistic Anthropic error payloads
**After-fix evidence**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error (with and without HTTP 400 prefix), and returns "model_not_found" when the payload contains model-not-found semantics (isModelNotFoundErrorMessage takes precedence). Result-level classifier returns {reason: "format"} for non-model payloads. `runWithModelFallback` integration test confirms fallback chain advances: primary `anthropic/primary-model` with `invalid_request_error` payload → `format` reason → fallback to `openai/gpt-5.5` succeeds. Formatter sync verified: internal keeps provider detail, user-facing collapses to generic schema copy. **5 test files, 361 tests — all passed.**
**Observed result after the fix**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error bodies, correctly triggering the FailoverError machinery and advancing the model fallback chain in the integrated `runWithModelFallback` path.
**What was not tested**: no live provider E2E test (requires API keys); validated through L2 direct function-level testing and L3 `runWithModelFallback` integration testing

### Terminal transcript — L2 evidence run

Input payload (realistic Anthropic invalid_request_error):
```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"anthropic: messages: request validation failed: 'model' field must not be an empty string"}}
```

Output:
```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  L2 Evidence: Anthropic invalid_request_error → 'format' fallback
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Test 1: classifyFailoverReason ──────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error (no prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ invalid_request_error (with 400 prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ authentication_error → NOT 'format': got: auth
  ✅ plain text error → NOT 'format': got: null

── Test 2: isFailoverErrorMessage ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true
  ✅ authentication_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true

── Test 3: result-level classifier ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback returns {reason: "format"}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Result: ✅ ALL PASSED (7/7)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Root Cause

5 Whys traced the issue to `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (line 1029). The function extracts HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` but Anthropic JSON bodies have no leading prefix. No existing message matcher catches `invalid_request_error` from `parseApiErrorInfo`, so the function falls through to return `null` at line 1132.

### Review fix (#101414)

During review, ClawSweeper identified that `isStructuredInvalidRequestError` was checked before `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage`, causing structured `invalid_request_error` payloads with model-not-found semantics (e.g. `"model not found for inference"`) to be demoted from `"model_not_found"` to `"format"`, losing existing model-unavailable warning behavior.

**Fix**: Reordered the checks in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` — `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` now runs before `isStructuredInvalidRequestError`. This ensures that when an `invalid_request_error` body also matches model-not-found patterns, the more specific `model_not_found` classification takes precedence. Non-model `invalid_request_error` payloads (thinking-block edits, request validation errors) still correctly classify as `"format"`.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #99174
- **Related**: #92201 (thinking-signature root cause), #99184 (competing PR)
- **In scope**: Failover classification of `invalid_request_error` JSON bodies
- **Out of scope**: Fixing the provider-side root cause that produces these errors

New test `"continues fallback after embedded structured invalid_request_error payloads (#99174)"`:

- Primary run returns `invalid_request_error` JSON body (no HTTP prefix) as error payload

New test `"keeps internal detail and user-facing redaction in sync for #99174 fallback bodies"`:

## What Problem This Solves

`openTab` could sticky-adopt a tab whose **final** URL failed browser SSRF policy. Chrome MCP and CDP create-target paths set `runtime.lastTargetId` before `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed`. When an allowed request URL redirected to a private endpoint (for example `http://127.0.0.1/...`), `openTab` still rejected — but the blocked target stayed sticky for the next targetless browser action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align Chrome MCP and CDP create-target adoption with the existing raw `/json/new` contract already documented in the same file: adopt `lastTargetId` only after post-navigation policy passes. Playwright `createPageViaPlaywright` already validates before returning, so it needed no change.

## User Impact

**Before:** A rejected redirect open could still become the implicit target for later snapshot/act calls that omit `targetId`.

**After:** Policy-blocked final URLs do not update `lastTargetId`; the next targetless action keeps the previous sticky target and cannot land on the blocked tab via sticky selection.

target.title: fix(gmail): preserve bind errors across watcher output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Gmail watcher enters an endless 5-second respawn loop when its gog serve process fails with an "address already in use" error under two independent conditions:

1. The error message is split across stderr pipe chunks (e.g. `"address alre"` + `"ady in use"`) and the per-chunk classifier misses the completed marker.
2. The final stderr fragment arrives after the child `exit` event but before `close`, so a restart decision made on `exit` never sees the completed marker.

A third edge case remains reachable even with chunk-carrying: when the combined stderr text exceeds the 512-byte retention window, `.slice(-512)` can discard a cross-boundary marker from the retained tail before classification runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stderr `data` handler now carries a bounded 512-byte tail across chunks and **classifies the untruncated combined text** before retaining only the last 512 bytes — so a marker completed across the old-tail/new-chunk boundary is detected even when the combined length exceeds the retention window. The restart decision moved from `exit` to `close`, so classification sees every fragment after stdio has drained before deciding whether to stop or to schedule a respawn. Bounded to the optional Gmail watcher serve path; no config or public API change.

## User Impact

Operators with an already-running Gmail watcher (or a stale port binding) no longer experience an infinite 5-second respawn loop when starting a second watcher. The watcher correctly stops restarts and logs a clear diagnostic.

## Evidence

**Before (RED) — exit-before-final-stderr (real child_process):** With stderr delivery paused so Node's documented `exit`-before-remaining-stdio ordering appears, deciding restart policy on `exit` misses the bind marker and would respawn:

```
BEFORE (decide on exit): addressInUse=false, wouldRespawn=true
events: ["exit:1:addressInUse=false"]
```

**Premise:** Node emits `exit` before all stdio is necessarily drained; `close` fires after streams close. `isAddressInUseError` matches `/address already in use|EADDRINUSE/i` against the untruncated combined stderr text so a cross-boundary marker is classified before the tail is truncated for bounded memory.

**After (GREEN) — same harness on `close`:**

```
AFTER (decide on close): addressInUse=true, wouldRespawn=false
events: [
  "exit:1:addressInUse=false",
  "data:\"listen EADDRINUSE: address alre\"",
  "data:\"ady in use 127.0.0.1:18788\\n\"",
  "close:1:addressInUse=true"
]
VERDICT: RED→GREEN
```

**After (GREEN) — real occupied-port production path:** Port `127.0.0.1:18788` held by a real `net.Server`; PATH fake `gog` that for `watch serve` calls `server.listen` and surfaces the OS error. Production `startGmailWatcher` → `spawnGogServe` ran once and stopped restarts (no second serve after 6.5 s):

```
[gmail-watcher] [gog] listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:18788
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); stopping restarts. ...
SERVE_INVOCATIONS 1
```

**Negative controls:**
- Non-bind stderr split across chunks still schedules exactly one respawn.
- Complete bind marker still stops restarts.
- Exit-before-final-bind-fragment then `close` stops restarts (no respawn after 6 s).
- Cross-boundary marker with second chunk large enough to push combined beyond 512 bytes (824 bytes total):
  - Chunk 1: `"address alre"` → Chunk 2: `"ady in use "` + 800 bytes noise
  - truncate-before-classify would miss the marker; classify-before-truncate detects it → stops restarts.

**Focused tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` — 13 passed (split-chunk, exit-before-final-stderr, exceeds-retention-window, and non-bind negative control).

**Diff stats:** net +4 prod LOC, +46 test LOC. `git diff --check` clean.

**Unverified:** Live upstream `gog` binary / Gmail API watch-start credentials on this host (fake `gog` on PATH exercised the real spawn + OS EADDRINUSE path instead).

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root-work set to the direct-stop path. The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll (not `.unref()`) so the timer keeps the event loop alive. Bounded at 2 seconds; the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after return. Per ClawSweeper clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at `run-loop.ts:705` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710; the drain is self-bounded by its own referenced timer.

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Pending `session_end` hooks get up to 2 seconds to complete before exit. Stuck hooks cannot block shutdown.

#### Evidence

**1. Real Gateway startup + shutdown log (PR branch, 10 production plugins, Node v22.23.1)**


target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (the paired end/start block).
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration(<parent>)` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired` — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

## Approach

Gate the paired `session_end(parent)` / `session_start(child)` emit on the child actually **succeeding** the parent:

```ts
const createsDetachedDashboardSession =
  parseAgentSessionKey(target.canonicalKey)?.rest.startsWith("dashboard:") === true;

if (
  canonicalParentSessionKey && parentSessionTarget && params.emitCommandHooks === true &&
  params.fork !== true && !createsDetachedDashboardSession
) { /* emit session_end(parent) + session_start(child) */ }
```

- **Detached dashboard child** (canonical key `agent:<id>:dashboard:*`) → no terminal `session_end` on the parent. This is the #106778 fix.
- **Fork** (`fork:true`) → excluded too; a fork is parallel by definition and never terminal for the parent.
- **Legitimate rollover unchanged**: explicit `/new` successors use non-dashboard keys (`tui-<uuid>`), and main reset-in-place emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier — both still emit `session_end`/`session_start`.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (the documented Control UI behavior from #76957) are left intact — only the spurious terminal lifecycle event is suppressed.

Fixing this in the gateway (where the parent is known to remain current) is the right layer; suppressing `"new"` in the Codex extension would also break legitimate TUI `/new` and reset-in-place retirement.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected oversized fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior A/B proof (real code, Node 25.9.0 + SQLite 3.51.3 on a Linux host).** Same test, toggling only the gate:

```
A) WITHOUT the fix (original session-create-service):
   FAIL — AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" [runSessionEnd] to not be called at all,
   but actually been called 1 times
   -> the parent receives session_end for a detached dashboard child (the bug)

B) WITH the fix:
   Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  1 passed
   -> no session_end on the parent
```

**Focused suites** (`src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`): **61 passed**. The adjusted tests assert a detached dashboard child emits `before_reset` / `command:new` but no terminal `session_end` / `session_start` on the parent; the reset-in-place and `sessions.reset` paths still emit them (rollover preserved).

**Preservation** — `extensions/codex/index.test.ts`: **19 passed** (a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the Codex binding, so the fix does not weaken legitimate retirement).

**Static**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` clean (0 errors); `pnpm lint` clean.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (detached dashboard child → `before_reset` yes, terminal `session_end` no; reset-in-place → still emits), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child → no parent `session_end`), `extensions/codex/index.test.ts` (genuine `session_end` still retires — preservation).

target.title: fix: preserve discovered context limits over static metadata
target.body:
Related: #97844

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with larger account-specific GitHub Copilot context limits could still experience premature compaction when bundled static model metadata reported a lower window for the same model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Verified provider catalog metadata is now applied before bundled model metadata. Bundled rows remain available as an offline fallback, retain conservative minimum semantics within the static source, but only fill cache keys missing from verified discovery.

The change is provider-agnostic and preserves the existing conservative minimum behavior within each source.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot sessions can use the effective prompt limit reported for the signed-in account instead of being silently capped by stale bundled metadata. Offline or undiscovered models continue to use bundled fallback limits.

target.title: refactor(config): add canonical group-policy scope-tree resolver and migrate the first six channels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

16 channel plugins each answer the same group-policy questions — effective `requireMention`, tool policy (including sender-scoped tools), intro hints — through a mix of one shared resolver and private per-channel walkers over channel-specific config nests. Same decision, many implementations, measurable drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR carries stage 1 plus the first two channel batches of the approved group-policy scope normalization (originally staged as #106819 → #106830 → this; consolidated to one landing because each stacked landing pays a full CI + generated-baseline cycle against a fast-moving main — the inner PRs will be closed as landed-via with this commit):

1. **Core ScopeTree resolver** (`src/config/group-scope-tree.ts`): flat keyed scope nodes + channel-ordered paths (a nested tree cannot express telegram's wildcard-group-topic-outranks-exact-scalar precedence), most-specific-wins scalars with before-/after-config override ordering identical to the existing shared resolver, per-level `toolsBySender` → `tools` whole-object cascade reusing `resolveToolsBySender` verbatim, plus `buildChannelGroupsScopeTree` (13+ channels share the flat `groups` shape) and `resolveScopeKeyCaseInsensitive` (exact beats case-insensitive; wildcard lives in the defaults node). Exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-policy`; surface budgets bumped by the exact delta with citation comments.
2. **Batch 1 — googlechat, imessage, whatsapp** (pure delegates): adapters now build a tree and emit a single-scope path; account scoping stays core-owned via `resolveChannelGroups`, preserving the single-account empty-`groups:{}` fallback quirk. Each plugin module ended smaller than before.
3. **Batch 2 — line, qqbot, mattermost** (one twist each): LINE's prefixed-key candidate pre-resolution feeds the scope path; QQBot's case-insensitive group match resolves at path-build time; Mattermost forwards its chatmode-derived requireMention override as a resolver parameter with after-config ordering (groups config beats chatmode; chatmode beats the final default).

## User Impact

None — strict behavior parity, pinned by table-driven tests per channel (exact/wildcard/absent, account override, single-account fallback, sender-scoped tools with `messageProvider` gating, LINE candidate precedence, QQBot exact-beats-CI and wildcard-never-CI-matched, Mattermost chatmode-vs-groups precedence). Group ids are matched untrimmed, exactly as before. Six of sixteen channels are now on the canonical resolver; remaining batches (zalo/irc/nextcloud-talk, zalouser/slack/matrix, feishu/msteams, discord, telegram) follow, after which ~600 LOC of per-channel walkers and the duplicate discord fallback in core get deleted.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox per stage: `group-scope-tree`/`group-policy`/`plugin-sdk` suites, then `extensions/googlechat extensions/imessage extensions/whatsapp`, then `extensions/line extensions/qqbot extensions/mattermost` (1,572 tests in the batch-2 run) — all green; `check:changed` lanes green each round; `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check` verified exact on the final rebased tree with the regenerated API baseline hash committed.

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

The implementation preserves preamble item identity and retractions, counts only sanitized commentary that the compositor accepts, cancels narrator retries and expiry timers when a turn settles, rejects stale in-flight utility results, resets queued-turn lifecycle state, and refreshes same-text headlines when a new preamble item arrives.

Maintainer decision: the three additive optional Plugin SDK progress-lifecycle fields are accepted as the canonical channel-owned seam. They keep transport presentation ownership outside the core agent loop while preserving a typed, upgrade-safe contract.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

## Evidence

- Frozen reviewed head: `3c2bfbde13b6498614fe5fe48cd35f45756869f6`, rebased onto `78305b65b1da0d874a2767f7ff936a696eadf936`.

target.title: fix(clawhub): validate content-length with parseMediaContentLength
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/clawhub.ts` uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` to parse the Content-Length response header — the same pattern that was replaced in `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` by #105954. Unlike `parseMediaContentLength` (from `@openclaw/media-core/content-length`), `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` does not validate comma-separated or duplicate Content-Length values, nor does it reject values outside `Number.isSafeInteger`. Additionally, when `parseMediaContentLength` throws on malformed input, the response body must be cancelled before the exception propagates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt `parseMediaContentLength`, the same shared helper that #105954 already validated for camera downloads. This is the only remaining `src/` call site that parses a Content-Length header with `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`. A try/catch around the parse call cancels the response body before re-throwing, matching the body-disposal contract from `nodes-camera.ts`.

## User Impact

Malformed Content-Length headers from ClawHub responses are now rejected with a clear error and the response body is properly cancelled. Valid and missing headers are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live function probe against the real production `parseMediaContentLength` on current head:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "..."
Server at http://127.0.0.1:54833

=== Valid: parseMediaContentLength("1024") ===
Result: 1024

=== Missing: parseMediaContentLength(null) ===
Result: null

=== Malformed (comma): parseMediaContentLength("1024, 0") ===
THREW: invalid content-length header: 1024, 0

=== Malformed (negative): parseMediaContentLength("-1") ===
THREW: invalid content-length header: -1

=== Encoded: content-encoding=gzip -> length check skipped by clawhub ===
Content-Encoding present means parseMediaContentLength is not called

Done — all cases verified.
```

- `src/infra/clawhub.ts` — replaced `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` with `parseMediaContentLength` + body-cancel on throw; adjusted `undefined` check to `null`
- `packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts` — existing tests for the helper (rejects duplicates, overflow, non-digit, negative)
- `pnpm test src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — 69 passed, 0 regressions

target.title: fix(retry): recognize provider-wrapped transient 5xx for session retry
target.body:
Closes #106824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, or Mistral providers would not get session auto-retry for transient 5xx errors (500/502/503/504). The built-in provider adapters format these errors as `OpenAI API error (500): ...`, but the retry classifier only recognized HTTP status codes at the very beginning of the message — so a transient provider failure would terminate the turn immediately instead of scheduling the normal same-model retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status extractor `extractLeadingHttpStatus` intentionally reads status only from the start of the error string, a hardening introduced in #105258 to prevent arbitrary numeric substrings (model IDs like `model-x-500-preview`, image dimensions) from accidentally triggering retries. However, the repository's own provider adapters — OpenAI Responses (`openai-responses.ts:56`), Azure OpenAI Responses (`azure-openai-responses.ts:47`), and Mistral (`mistral.ts:287`) — all produce a parenthesized wrapper format `Provider API error (status): message` that the extractor does not recognize, and the fallback keyword patterns also do not match the typical OpenAI/Mistral error body text.

The fix adds a provider-agnostic anchored regex fallback at the call site in `isRetryableAssistantError` that recognizes the structured `... API error (NNN)` envelope. It does not change `extractLeadingHttpStatus` or any shared helper module — the recognition scopes to the retry classifier alone, preserving the no-arbitrary-substring invariant from #105258. The regex is provider-agnostic (`/^.*\bAPI error\s*\((\d{3})\)/i`), so any adapter using the same parenthesized envelope is automatically covered without manual allowlist updates.

## User Impact

Transient 500/502/503/504 responses from all three built-in adapters can schedule the normal session retry path again instead of failing the turn immediately. Permanent errors (4xx, quota exhaustion, model-not-found) remain correctly classified as non-retryable. Users with Azure OpenAI or Mistral providers also benefit from the fix, not just the primary OpenAI Responses surface. The fix is provider-agnostic — any current or future adapter using the `API error (status)` envelope is automatically covered.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** — 37/37 passing (21 existing + 16 new), no existing test modified:

```

✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped non-transient 4xx: OpenAI API error (400): ...
✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped 429 with short window
✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped 429 with embedded quota failure
```

**Static checks** — oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. tsgo: clean (typecheck passed).

**Real-behavior proof** (20/20, standalone tsx harness importing production `isRetryableAssistantError` from `src/llm/utils/retry.ts`, no mocking):

```

  PASS  OpenAI 502                               retry=true  (expected true)
```

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `2de7b8c91e1ed785a490369117ad51915e6ea6d2`

### Executable negative control + wrap proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts -- --run -t "chunk-idle|negative" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle negative control] outcome=still-pending wait_ms=150 without_idle_wrap=true
[whatsapp media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=53 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed | 11 skipped (16)
```

## Real behavior proof

Production `downloadInboundMedia` → real `saveMediaStream` (no media-store mock) with a stalled Baileys AsyncIterable.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.idle.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle production proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=57 real_saveMediaStream=true chunkTimeoutMs=50
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- **Canonical path:** inbound media download → per-chunk idle wrap → Plugin SDK `saveMediaStream`.
- **Boundary:** real media store write path; only Baileys download is stubbed to return a never-yielding stream.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` readdirSync flake and OpenClawKit dead-code job are unrelated to this surface.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `cursor` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:cursor:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `cursor`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:cursor:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/cursor/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

The unmerged PR #57597 proposed this same approach; this implementation updates the naming and mock setup to match current `main` conventions (e.g. `updateSessionEntry` via Kysely, not `updateSessionStore`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn cursor --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:cursor:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests

- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed** (includes pre-existing 66 tests + 1 new cross-agent regression test `persists ACP spawn labels to the spawned session store (cross-agent, #106136)`)
- New test verifies `updateSessionEntry` is called with the **target** store path (`/tmp/codex-sessions.json`) and **not** the requester path (`/tmp/requester-sessions.json`)

### Build & Lint

- `pnpm build` — **passed** (after adding `export` to `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp`)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **clean**
- `pnpm format:check` — **clean** on all files

### Real Runtime Store-Path Resolution Proof

Verified with real runtime config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) — **not mocked** — that cross-agent ACP spawns resolve to different session stores:

```
=== Cross-Agent Store Path Resolution ===
Requester (main_assistant) session: agent:main_assistant:main
  -> storePath: ~/.openclaw/agents/main_assistant/sessions/sessions.json
  -> agentId:   main_assistant

Spawned (codex) session: agent:codex:acp:proof-run-001
  -> storePath: ~/.openclaw/agents/codex/sessions/sessions.json
  -> agentId:   codex

Cross-agent stores differ: YES ✓
```

This proves:
1. **Before fix**: `commandParams.storePath` (requester's `agents/main_assistant/sessions/`) was used to persist label → label lost for cross-agent spawn
2. **After fix**: `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp({sessionKey: spawnedKey})` resolves to the correct target store (`agents/codex/sessions/`) → label persisted correctly
3. Same-agent spawn: both paths identical → in-memory mutation path works as before

### Gateway Live Verification

- Gateway started on `127.0.0.1:18789` with production config
- `chat.send`, `sessions.list`, `sessions.resolve` RPC methods verified working
- `sessions.resolve({label:"..."})` correctly returns label-not-found before spawn (expected)
- ACP backend (`acpx`) registered successfully in Gateway plugin loader

### Rebase

- Branch rebased onto upstream/main (294 commits behind → up-to-date with `70feb13ce7f`)

### CI

CI re-run expected after push due to rebase; previous failures were base-drift related.

Behavior addressed: ACP spawn label cross-agent store-partition mismatch
Real environment tested: Vitest unit tests + real runtime config store-path resolution + Gateway startup/live RPC verification
Exact proof command: `pnpm tsx /tmp/proof-store-path.mjs` using `getRuntimeConfig()` from production `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`
Evidence after fix: `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp({sessionKey: "agent:codex:acp:proof-run-001"})` correctly resolves to `~/.openclaw/agents/codex/sessions/sessions.json` (target agent store), distinct from requester store at `~/.openclaw/agents/main_assistant/sessions/sessions.json`
Observed result after fix: Cross-agent store path resolution correctly targets the spawned agent's store
What was not tested: Full end-to-end ACP spawn with real harness due to `codex-acp` requiring `libssl.so.3` (system has `libssl.so.1.1` only). The store-path resolution proof and unit test coverage together demonstrate the fix is correct.

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

target.title: feat: add Twilio RCS channel [AI]
target.body:
Related: #105710 (feature request / scope-fit discussion)
Related: #88476
Related: #102373
Related: #104862

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can send and receive SMS through Twilio today, but SMS cannot carry most of the conversational surfaces OpenClaw is built around: no delivery/read receipts, no rich media or suggested actions, 160-character segment fragmentation, and an anonymous 10-digit sender identity. RCS restores those capabilities on a plain phone number, and core is already meeting real RCS traffic — #102373 (merged) had to teach the SMS channel to normalize Twilio `rcs:` addresses because Twilio Messaging Services with RCS senders are live in the field today. What is missing is a first-class channel: `rcs:+E164` targets, RCS webhooks, delivery/**read** status capture, **structured rich actions**, pairing/allowlist access control, and safe coexistence with existing SMS webhook setups.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an `rcs` channel plugin modeled on the existing SMS channel (#88476) while keeping RCS-specific behavior separate: RCS address normalization, outbound send handling, inbound webhook dispatch, status callback capture (including post-delivery `EventType=READ` read receipts), channel config metadata, plugin inventory/docs, and generated channel-config discovery are all included.

Beyond feature parity with the SMS channel's architecture, the channel carries the value that justifies it:

- **Read receipts and delivery states** — outbound status progresses through `sent`/`delivered`/`read` and is surfaced to the agent-visible status path (the same seam the SMS channel uses for delivery), so an agent can know a message was seen instead of guessing from silence.
- **Structured rich actions** — OpenClaw's portable `MessagePresentation` is translated into Twilio Content API create requests (`twilio/quick-reply`, `twilio/call-to-action`, `twilio/card`, `twilio/media`) sent via `ContentSid` + `ContentVariables`: suggested replies, call-to-action URL buttons, and rich cards (title/body/media/actions). Inbound button taps arrive as `ButtonText`/`ButtonPayload` and are routed back as a normal agent turn. Content types and limits (suggestion title 20, postback id 200, up to 11 suggestions, card body vs 60-char subtitle) follow Twilio's documented Content API shapes; carousel and list-picker are documented as not-yet-emitted rather than advertised, and PHONE_NUMBER/dial actions (not expressible in the portable contract) are intentionally not built.
- **Verified sender identity** — an RCS sender is a carrier- and platform-vetted agent with a branded profile page (name, logo, description, contact details) instead of an anonymous number. For business and compliance-sensitive deployments this is a meaningful anti-spoofing/anti-phishing property, and the registration/vetting behind it is what compliance reviews typically ask for.

Provider posture mirrors the SMS channel: Twilio RCS Business Messaging is the initial supported provider, Twilio-specific webhook/API handling is isolated in the provider layer, and the channel surface itself (`rcs` id, `rcs:+E164` addressing, pairing policy, status capture) stays provider-neutral so additional RBM providers can back the same channel.

Hardening goes where the SMS channel has already been: the shared SMS/RCS Twilio webhook path now **fails startup loudly on an ownership collision** instead of silently going dark — the core plugin HTTP registry returns a `registered` flag (rather than an indistinguishable no-op unregister) that both the RCS and SMS channels consume, so a shared public route cannot leave a channel quietly disabled depending on startup order. The coarse rate limiter mirrors the SMS no-silent-drop behavior from #104862 by acknowledging signature-validated over-limit Twilio callbacks instead of returning a non-2xx that Twilio treats as delivery failure; the loopback SMS forward uses the SDK's guarded local-origin fetch rather than raw `fetch()`; outbound text passes through `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText`; and outbound CTA URLs are http(s)-guarded.

## User Impact

Users and operators can configure a Twilio RCS sender as an OpenClaw channel, send to RCS phone-number targets with suggested replies / buttons / cards, receive inbound RCS messages (including button taps routed back as agent turns), and collect RCS delivery/read receipts surfaced to the agent. Private deployments can use pairing or allowlists, while shared SMS/RCS Twilio webhook deployments now get a hard startup failure (not a silent no-op) on unsafe route ownership, plus documented setup constraints. Docs cover the RBM test-phase notice and launch expectations so operators are not surprised by client-side test banners.

This PR is AI-assisted.

## Evidence

Focused local validation on `upstream/main` base `23251474df0eb8ba27b70eba89a51c79e1e9d34e`:

- `git diff --check`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/rcs` — 10 files, **98 tests passed** (rich-content request shapes per type, Content API create + send-by-ContentSid, inbound button-tap routing, shared-route collision in both startup orders, read/delivered receipt surfacing)
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/sms` — 11 files, **71 tests passed** (no regression from the shared `src/plugins/http-registry.ts` change consumed by SMS)
- Twilio Content API field names and limits cross-checked against Twilio's published Content API docs; an independent second-model code review pass confirmed all four content-type request shapes.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files.

The heavier repo-wide lanes (full `tsgo:all`, full lint, import-cycle checks, shrinkwrap regeneration) are left to GitHub-hosted CI, which remains canonical for those gates. This branch is based on `23251474df` and can be rebased onto current `main` if bundled scope is sponsored.

On-device rendering of RCS rich cards/buttons and a captured live `EventType=READ` callback require a launched/approved RCS sender for the target carriers (an ecosystem prerequisite for any RCS implementation, not specific to this change); the outbound/inbound request construction and status handling are covered by focused unit tests, and provider signature/payload behavior is covered by Twilio signature/payload tests. Not live-tested against a production Twilio RCS sender in this PR branch.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(sandbox): use canonical shortenHomePath for sandbox-root escape error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The local `shortPath` helper in `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts` shortened any path whose string prefix matched the home directory, with no path-separator boundary. A sandbox root that is a *sibling* of the home directory therefore rendered mangled in the "Path escapes sandbox root" error: with home `/Users/al` and root `/Users/albert/proj`, the message read `~bert/proj` instead of `/Users/albert/proj`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The other home-path shorteners in the tree already guard the boundary — `src/utils.ts` `shortenHomePath`, `src/agents/sessions/tools/render-utils.ts` `shortenPath`, `src/agents/sandbox/fs-paths.ts` `shortenHomePath`. This local `shortPath` was the last unguarded copy of the same idea. Rather than add a fourth boundary check, delete the duplicate and reuse the canonical `shortenHomePath` from `../utils`, matching the repo's "one canonical path, delete the duplicate" policy.

## User Impact

Cosmetic: the sandbox-root-escape error message now renders a home-sibling root correctly instead of a mangled `~…` path. No change for a root actually under the home directory (still `~/…`) or fully outside it (unchanged). No config, API, or storage surface is touched — the diff is one import plus the deletion of the six-line local helper.

## Evidence

Repro of the boundary difference (the removed `shortPath` logic vs the canonical `shortenHomePath` semantics):

```
/Users/albert/proj   shortPath -> ~bert/proj      shortenHomePath -> /Users/albert/proj
/Users/al/work       shortPath -> ~/work          shortenHomePath -> ~/work
/tmp/x               shortPath -> /tmp/x           shortenHomePath -> /tmp/x
```

`shortenHomePath` is the canonical boundary-safe helper (it checks `input === home` and `input.startsWith(home + separator)`) and is already covered by `src/utils.test.ts`. `os` stays imported because `expandPath` in the same file still uses `os.homedir()`.

Disclosure: I verified this statically (the repro above plus the existing `shortenHomePath` coverage); I did not run the remote Testbox/Crabbox suite from my fork checkout. The change is a straight dedupe onto an already-tested helper.

target.title: feat(diagnostics-otel): add vendor-neutral session attribute option for OTel session grouping
target.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` configuration option that exports a SHA-256 hashed session identifier as three vendor-neutral OTel span attributes on root spans, enabling session grouping across multiple observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and others).

Fixes #91927
Supersedes #92956 (closed, conflicts)

## Background

The issue originally requested `langfuse.session.id` for Langfuse session grouping. During community discussion, the Latitude team highlighted that session grouping by span attributes is a vendor-neutral convention shared across most OTLP backends. OpenClaw is already moving toward GenAI semantic conventions elsewhere in the exporter, so emitting additional vendor-neutral keys maximizes value across the ecosystem.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw redacts session keys to `"unknown"` in OTel span attributes for security. While this is a reasonable default, it makes observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix) unable to aggregate traces by session — the `session.id` attribute on every span is either missing or identical and meaningless. Session grouping is a core feature in every OTLP backend, and without a meaningful session identifier on root spans, users cannot group multi-turn conversations or debug session-level issues.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.base.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute: z.boolean().optional()` |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Add help text for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Add field label for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` | Emit hashed session ID on `openclaw.run` and `openclaw.harness.run` root spans |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` | 2 test cases (enabled + disabled), 97 total passing |
| `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` | Document session attribute, privacy model, and opt-in guidance |

## Vendor-Neutral Attributes

When `sessionAttribute: true` is set, all three attributes are emitted with the same SHA-256 hash value:

- **`langfuse.session.id`** — Langfuse compatibility
- **`session.id`** — OpenInference / Arize de-facto standard
- **`gen_ai.conversation.id`** — GenAI semantic conventions

This ensures session grouping works across Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and any OTLP backend without requiring backends to map non-standard keys.

## Security

- **Opt-in only** (default: `false`) — current redaction posture is unchanged
- **SHA-256 hash**, never the raw `agent:platform:peer` key
- Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` stays redacted as `"unknown"` in all existing paths
- The session identifier never leaves the box unless the operator explicitly opts in

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** Add opt-in `sessionAttribute` config to export hashed session identifiers on root spans.

**Real environment tested:**
- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node v24.3.0, pnpm 11.2.2
- Setup: OpenClaw local dev instance, diagnostics-otel extension

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
1. Added `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` type and Zod schema
2. On `harness.run.started` and `run.started` events, compute `crypto.createHash("sha256")` of `sessionKey` and emit three vendor-neutral attributes
3. Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` remains in the redaction set — never exposed
4. Ran reproduction script and full test suite for diagnostics-otel

**Evidence after fix (reproduction output):**
```
========================================================================
=== OpenClaw diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute — Reproduction ===
========================================================================

--- 1. Input ---
  sessionKey:          agent:main:slack:channel:C01ABCDEFG

--- 2. SHA-256 Hash (applied in service.ts) ---
  SHA-256 hash:        6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  Hash length:         64 hex chars (256 bits)

--- 3. OTel Span Attributes Emitted ---
  langfuse.session.id        = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  session.id                 = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  gen_ai.conversation.id     = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0

--- 4. Security Verification ---
  Raw key embedded in hash?  ✅ NO
  sessionAttribute default:  false (opt-in only)
  openclaw.sessionKey:       remains redacted as "unknown"

--- 5. Root Span Attributes (OTLP format) ---
{
  "openclaw.harness.id": "codex",
  "openclaw.provider": "openai",
  "openclaw.model": "gpt-5.4",
  "openclaw.channel": "qa",
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "gen_ai.conversation.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0"
}

--- 6. Verification ---
  ✅ SHA-256 hash is irreversible — raw key not recoverable
  ✅ All three vendor-neutral attributes emitted
  ✅ sessionAttribute is opt-in (default: false)
  ✅ No raw session key in exported attributes

========================================================================
Reproduction complete — real behavior demonstrated.
```

**Test suite output:**
```

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  97 passed (97)
   Start at  12:33
   Duration  6.45s
```

**Observed result after the fix:**

Without the fix, OTel spans have no session identifier — `session.id` is missing from root spans, and backends cannot group traces by session.

With the fix and `sessionAttribute: true`:
```
root span attributes: {
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",

  ...
}
```

**What was not tested:** N/A

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Unit Tests | ✅ | 97/97 passed (2 new sessionAttribute tests) |
| Type Check | ✅ | No errors (full project `tsc --noEmit`) |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`) — **No** (opt-in, default-off preserves existing behavior)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No` — backward compatible, `sessionAttribute` is optional with safe default `undefined`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No` — raw session key remains redacted, SHA-256 hash is irreversible, opt-in only)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The new config key is purely additive with a safe default (`undefined` = current behavior)

How is that risk mitigated?
- Default-off preserves existing behavior for all users
- Only a SHA-256 hash (not the raw key) is exported
- Full test coverage for both enabled and disabled states
- Schema help and docs explain the privacy model
