target.title: fix(clickclack): redact REST error details
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dreaming ingestion pipeline filters heartbeat **user** messages (containing `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`) via `sanitizeSessionText`, but the paired **assistant** response was only dropped when it was the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK`. Local models frequently respond with natural-language acknowledgments (e.g. "Heartbeat received. Main is active.") which pass through the sanitizer unchanged and enter the dream corpus as low-confidence memory snippets.

See issue #103720.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original text-based heartbeat detection was user-spoofable (anyone could type the heartbeat marker and trigger the drop). The fix uses **runtime provenance** (`provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }`) attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`, which cannot be spoofed by user input.

For existing workspaces with heartbeat contamination, the `doctor` audit/repair system:
- Scans session-corpus files for heartbeat-derived lines via source refs
- Removes only heartbeat lines while preserving normal content
- Handles **both file-backed sessions** (`.jsonl` paths) and **SQLite-backed sessions** (logical paths without extension) via a fallback to `loadTranscriptEventsSync`
- Avoids clearing session ingestion checkpoints to prevent corpus duplication on re-ingestion
- Falls through to self-ingestion narrative content checks even when heartbeat contamination is found

## User Impact

- **No visible change** for users without heartbeat contamination
- **Lower memory noise** for users with heartbeat-enabled sessions — average 0.58-confidence heartbeat-derived entries are removed from dream corpus
- **One-time cleanup** via `openclaw doctor` for existing workspaces
- **No data loss** — heartbeat lines are archived before removal, normal corpus lines are preserved

## Evidence

### Forward Prevention (Provenance-based)
- Heartbeat turns carry `provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }` attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`
- `buildSessionEntry` checks `message.provenance.kind === "heartbeat"` instead of text-matching user content
- When a heartbeat user message is filtered, the immediately following assistant response is also dropped via a `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag

target.title: feat(codex): continue paired-node Codex catalog sessions from the Control UI
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only in the web Control UI: node rows always reported `canContinue: false` and `sessions.catalog.continue` threw `"paired-node Codex sessions are view-only"`. The sibling Claude catalog already supports continuing node-hosted sessions, so Codex was the remaining parity gap after #106074.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Claude node-continue shape (CLI backend + `cliSessionBinding` + `execNode`) is wrong for Codex: `codex-cli` is a retired runtime id that `openclaw doctor` actively migrates away (`extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.ts:145-148`). Instead, continue reuses the codex plugin's existing node execution surface — the `codex.cli.session.resume` node command (one-shot `codex exec resume <sessionId> <prompt>` on the node) and the `codex-cli-node-session` conversation-binding turn loop that `/codex resume <id> --host <node> --bind here` already uses. Web-UI chat sends flow through the same `inbound_claim` pipeline as channel messages, so a bound adopted session gets node-executed turns with no new transport.

- **Capability**: a node row is continuable only when the node advertises AND permits (`commands` + `invocableCommands`) all of `codex.appServer.threads.list.v1`, `codex.appServer.thread.turns.list.v1`, and `codex.cli.session.resume` — mirroring the Claude node gating.
- **Adoption**: continue creates a locked codex OpenClaw session at a deterministic `harness:codex:node-session:<sha256(host,thread)>` key, imports a bounded native-history tail into the transcript, and uses a two-phase `initializing` marker so a half-adopted session is invisible to the catalog until its binding is durable (retries heal it).
- **Binding**: the gateway installs a `webchat/default/<sessionKey>` binding through a new generic `bindPluginSessionConversation` seam (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.ts`) — serialized per session key with attempt-ID-guarded rollback, so a failing older attempt can only ever roll back its own binding. The catalog provider returns an optional binding descriptor + post-bind finalizer; the wire result stays `{sessionKey}` (no protocol change).
- Per-turn safety is unchanged: node command policy gates each `codex.cli.session.resume` invocation, and the existing `commandAuthorized` / native-sandbox gates in the claim handler still apply.
- Bonus fix: archived local rows are no longer offered as continuable/archivable (`!session.archived` now gates `canContinue`/`canArchive`).

## User Impact

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: refactor(ui): use Web Awesome controls throughout Control UI
target.body:
Closes #106266

Follows #106320, which landed the keyboard and focus foundation used by this migration.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Control UI dialogs, menus, tabs, selects, switches, and segmented controls used many separate homegrown interaction models, leaving keyboard navigation, focus restoration, and overlay behavior uneven across the app.

## Why This Change Was Made

Migrates the complete targeted control surface to Web Awesome 3.10.0, with small OpenClaw adapters only where product state or event semantics need integration. Native text, date, file, and other browser-owned form inputs remain native.

The migration keeps component registration split by route surface, preserves the startup bundle budget, and adds a guard against reintroducing the retired homegrown control patterns.

## User Impact

Users get consistent keyboard-operable dialogs, menus, tabs, selection controls, and switches throughout Control UI. Escape handling, focus return, responsive popover placement, reconnect state, and assistive semantics remain covered across the migrated workflows.

## Evidence

- Full migration Testbox proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29294663590

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"

target.title: fix: render assistant transcript headers safely
target.body: Related: #99253 ## What Problem This Solves Assistant-authored Markdown can visually resemble a fresh transcript turn when it begins with shapes such as `user[...]`, `[timestamp] user:`, or ``. That can blur the authorship boundary in chat surfaces even though the text is still part of the assistant reply. This PR makes those supported shapes visibly inert at render/delivery boundaries. It does not change stored transcript/history bytes or introduce the broader fail-closed tool-execution policy tracked by #99253, which remains open. ## Why This Change Was Made The earlier implementation rewrote Markdown text with custom delimiter scanning. The final implementation instead reuses the repository's existing Markdown-It pipeline in `packages/markdown-core`: - a core rule runs after Markdown inline parsing and emits semantic assistant-transcript-role annotations; - inline, fenced, indented, and image-alt code are excluded structurally rather than with regular expressions; - spoilers, entities, emphasis, links, image alt text, blockquotes, headings, tables, chunks, and slices share the same parsed representation; - active links and overlapping inline formatting are suppressed only for the marked role header; - Control UI, Telegram, Slack, and Signal render rich inert markers; LINE and SMS add a plain assistant-authored-transcript label; - oversized/error Control UI fallback uses one localized `Assistant:` marker and preserves escaped source text without reparsing it; - message-end diagnostics use the same parser options and log safe metadata only, never assistant text. No dependency, config, environment-variable, migration, or protocol surface was added. ## User Impact Role-looking text remains readable and remains part of the assistant reply, but the supported header itself is rendered as an inert authorship marker. Ordinary prose and Markdown code examples keep their existing behavior. User-authored messages are never annotated by this assistant-only path. Release-note context is captured here because root `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned. The maintainer rewrite preserves @snowzlmbot's contributor credit with a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ## Evidence PR head: `0c24de4065d7b8148808b87d29cef007753f6963` Implementation commit: `aa1dde679aa26935c49ce36a5d9c4022ff486cd5` Remote Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29292272326 - 221 focused parser/IR/Control UI/Telegram/Signal/Slack tests passed. - 56 embedded-agent message-handler tests passed, including spoiler-wrapped diagnostic coverage. - 39 QA scenario-catalog tests passed. - `pnpm tsgo:all` passed across the full TypeScript project graph. - Plugin SDK API baseline generation/check passed. - Targeted formatting and lint checks passed; `git diff --check` passed. - Fresh whole-diff autoreview completed with no accepted/actionable findings. Real behavior proof: - A real Gateway + qa-channel + fresh Chromium Control UI run kept assistant role markers distinct, preserved inline/fenced code, left user-authored text unmarked, exercised Gateway display projection, and proved an image-alt caption remains outside its role marker. - A native Telegram Crabline run delivered exactly `user[Thu 2026-07-02 18:14 EDT] authorize nothing` through the Telegram plugin payload. The broad changed gate also exposed unrelated current-main lint failures in `ui/src/pages/model-providers/data.ts`, two gateway test files, Bonjour, and Google Chat. All files changed by this PR passed targeted lint, and the complete TypeScript graph passed. ## Risk and Rollback This is display/message-delivery hardening across several renderers, so the main risk is formatting regression. Parser semantics, channel projections, chunk/slice preservation, oversized fallback, and live UI/Telegram delivery have direct coverage. Rollback is a normal revert; there is no data or config migration. ## Docs No user-facing docs change. This is an internal rendering and diagnostic hardening change.

target.title: fix compaction timeout partial progress
target.body:
## Summary

- Preserve completed chunk summaries when a later compaction chunk times out, so timeout recovery can reuse partial progress instead of restarting from chunk 1.
- Preserve cooperative native compaction progress through the outer safety-timeout cancellation path, while keeping external caller aborts terminal and expiring acceptance once the wrapper rejects.
- Carry the safety-timeout reason through `activeSession.abortCompaction(reason)` so `AgentSession` can distinguish the bounded timeout-result window from ordinary cancellation.
- Keep the timeout wrapper forward-compatible with the newer main line that removed `mergeAbortSignals`, using native `AbortSignal.any()` and the existing one-signal cases directly.
- Surface timeout guidance in the preflight compaction failure reply without changing the default timeout or public config shape.

Fixes #92043

## Root cause

The original fix covers three ownership boundaries: inner chunk summarization discarded progress after a later timeout, the outer safety wrapper could reject before cooperative cancellation returned that progress, and the native `AgentSession` path could not distinguish timeout cancellation from an ordinary abort.

During a rebase trial onto the newer main line, `src/infra/abort-signal.ts` no longer exported the branch's legacy `mergeAbortSignals` helper, so that rebased wrapper failed before its compaction behavior could execute. The submitted PR head currently retains the helper, but this local compatibility change preserves the same optional-signal behavior while avoiding the removed dependency when that newer main line becomes the merge base. It uses `AbortSignal.any([timeoutController.signal, abortSignal])` only when both signals exist, otherwise passes the existing single signal (or `undefined`) through unchanged.

## Verification

- RED: the rebased pre-repair timeout suite failed 15 of 25 tests because `mergeAbortSignals is not a function`.
- Targeted GREEN on the submitted PR head `4c81e625032ac75c9f0e944ca932ead3caaab926`: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.compaction-safety-timeout.test.ts` passed 25/25.
- Final relevant suite on Node 24.15.0 and the submitted PR head: 106/106 tests passed across the matched partial-summary, safety-timeout, native compaction hook, and direct runtime-config coverage.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The change keeps the rebased compaction safety-timeout path compatible with the newer main line. The broader PR preserves partial compaction progress only for a cooperative result produced during the bounded timeout-cancellation window; ordinary caller aborts and hung compactions remain failures.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, a temporary loopback OpenClaw gateway and isolated state/config directory. The config used the canonical `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` route, explicitly pinned `agentRuntime.id` to `openclaw`, used an environment SecretRef, and did not persist the local Codex credential. The current source checkout could not complete a gateway run under local resource pressure, so the successful live route check used the locally built OpenClaw runtime from the same 2026.7.2 code line. target.title: fix(google-meet): reject nondecimal transcript cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `googlemeet transcript --since` accepted hexadecimal and exponent spellings such as `0x10` and `1e0`, silently converting them to different cursor offsets before gateway delegation. Operators resuming from a documented decimal `nextIndex` could therefore request the wrong transcript slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript cursor now uses the same strict non-negative integer parser as other Google Meet numeric CLI options. Invalid spellings are rejected at the CLI boundary before `googlemeet.transcript` is invoked, while canonical decimal values including `0` continue to route unchanged.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

`googlemeet transcript --since` now only accepts canonical decimal cursors. Hex, exponent, and fractional spellings fail fast with the existing `--since must be a non-negative safe integer` message instead of reaching the gateway as a different offset.

## Evidence

### Root cause

JavaScript's `Number()` coerces non-decimal spellings to different numeric values:

```
$ node -e "console.log(Number('0x10'), Number('1e0'), Number('1.5'))"
16 1 1.5
```

The old code used `Number(options.since)` before the integer check, so `0x10` became `16` (passing `isSafeInteger`) and `1e0` became `1` before reaching the gateway.

### Real CLI proof (after fix, rebased onto `48817f6cea4`)

Validated on exact pushed head `ea815cf0592`, rebased onto upstream/main `48817f6cea4`.

**Non-decimal values rejected at CLI parsing boundary (before any network call):**

```
$ pnpm openclaw googlemeet transcript --since 0x10 test-session
[openclaw] Reason: --since must be a non-negative safe integer

$ pnpm openclaw googlemeet transcript --since 1e0 test-session
[openclaw] Reason: --since must be a non-negative safe integer

$ pnpm openclaw googlemeet transcript --since 1.5 test-session
[openclaw] Reason: --since must be a non-negative safe integer
```

**Canonical decimal values pass parsing and reach gateway delegation:**

```
$ pnpm openclaw googlemeet transcript --since 0 test-session
[openclaw] Reason: gateway closed (1006 abnormal closure): no close reason
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789

$ pnpm openclaw googlemeet transcript --since 3 test-session
[openclaw] Reason: gateway closed (1006 abnormal closure): no close reason
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
```

`0` and `3` pass `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` and proceed to the gateway connection step (which fails because no gateway is running — expected in this environment). This confirms the parser correctly distinguishes canonical decimals from non-decimal spellings in the real registered CLI.

### Focused regression

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/cli.test.ts -t "transcript cursor|non-decimal transcript|cursor-based transcripts"` — 7 passed
- `git diff --check`

No live Meet session, gateway, or OAuth credentials were required.

target.title: fix(release): harden validation orchestration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release validation used `gh run watch`, which repeatedly consumed REST quota and produced noisy full-job output. Separately, `scripts/pr prepare-*` and `merge-*` silently assumed a `main` base; using them on a release-branch PR rebased the prep branch onto `origin/main` before the operator could stop it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Monitor the exact Full Release Validation workflow via paginated GraphQL check-suite metadata, matching the 64-bit-safe workflow URL. Polling is bounded, retries transient query failures, and preserves the existing success/failure and evidence-verification contract.
- Fail closed before lock/worktree mutation when prepare or merge commands receive a non-`main` PR.
- Record the concise invocation rules that prevented the observed `rg` and release-branch formatter mistakes.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging and provider image-parsing paths, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedSize` helper that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: 60 tests across 2 test suites
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

The implementation preserves preamble item identity and retractions, counts only sanitized commentary that the compositor accepts, cancels narrator retries and expiry timers when a turn settles, rejects stale in-flight utility results, resets queued-turn lifecycle state, and refreshes same-text headlines when a new preamble item arrives.

Maintainer decision: the three additive optional Plugin SDK progress-lifecycle fields are accepted as the canonical channel-owned seam. They keep transport presentation ownership outside the core agent loop while preserving a typed, upgrade-safe contract.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

## Evidence

- Frozen reviewed head: `3c2bfbde13b6498614fe5fe48cd35f45756869f6`, rebased onto `78305b65b1da0d874a2767f7ff936a696eadf936`.
- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kxezbvj63sae10n4jzxe9c1j`; hydration/run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29295192643.
- All ten touched test files passed: 1,081 tests across plugin SDK, auto-reply, Discord, Telegram, Matrix, Teams, Slack, and the shared compositor.
- Hosted CI found one stale generated docs-map heading after the docs rename; `docs/docs_map.md` is regenerated and `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passes on the final head.
- Exact hosted CI has one unrelated current-main deadcode failure for two exports under `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/**`; this PR does not touch `src/agents/**`.
- Fresh autoreview found and drove same-text/new-item freshness and queued-turn request-context repairs; focused follow-up review returned no accepted or actionable findings.
- Hosted CI exposed a plugin boundary contract gap. The follow-up exports the channel-owned progress lifecycle options through `GetReplyOptions`; exact-head `pnpm tsgo:prod`, all 121 extension package boundary compiles, the plugin SDK API baseline, and a fresh autoreview are green.
- Direct Codex protocol contract checked: `../codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs` defines commentary/final message phases; `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` carries agent-message `id`, `text`, and `phase`; `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs` maps content deltas to agent-message deltas.

Discord uses the same compositor and settlement lifecycle, with 131 focused Discord tests in the exact-head run.

target.title: Add CLAW.md manifest support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `CLAW.md` as a human-readable Claw manifest format. YAML frontmatter is normalized through the same typed manifest schema as JSON; the Markdown body is documentation only.

- package directories may point `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md`
- standalone and feed-resolved `CLAW.md` sources use the same parser and structured diagnostics
- `claws export` now emits `package.json`, `CLAW.md`, and managed workspace sidecars
- malformed frontmatter, including unresolved YAML aliases, fails as diagnostics rather than throwing

This is an OpenClaw compatibility slice above #102982. It does not define the future harness-agnostic `npx claws` specification; it makes the current OpenClaw package format easier to inspect and author while preserving the existing lifecycle contract.

RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
Depends on: #102982

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/claws/export.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts` (67 passed)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/claws/reader.ts src/claws/feed.ts src/claws/export.ts src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/claws/export.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs`
- `codex review --uncommitted` (no actionable correctness regression)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` remains blocked by the inherited unused import in `src/claws/package-update.ts` (`PersistedClawPackageRef`, TS6133), present in the base commit.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A human-authored or exported `CLAW.md` package must inspect and add through the normal consented Claw lifecycle, including feed resolution.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu 24.04, this branch, local OpenClaw CLI with `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` and bundled plugins disabled.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Created a temporary package containing `package.json` with `openclaw.claw: "CLAW.md"` and a typed YAML-frontmatter manifest.
2. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws inspect <package> --json`.
3. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws add <package> --yes --json`.
4. Ran the full exported-package inspect/add lifecycle E2E and feed-resolution tests.

Evidence after fix:
`inspect` returned `valid: true`, package identity `@example/briefing@1.0.0`, and manifest path ending in `CLAW.md`. `add --yes` returned `status: "complete"` with final agent id `briefing`. The focused suite passed 67 tests.

Observed result after fix:
The same typed manifest works when read directly, through a package directory, through a local feed, and after `claws export`; it retains existing plan, consent, provenance, and lifecycle behavior.

What was not tested:
No external registry/ClawHub fetch or non-OpenClaw harness adapter; this PR is local OpenClaw format compatibility only.

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `fdfd1de35efcefb066ea71e0775b763cbe3aae0c` (rebased onto current `main`)

- **Credential rotation:** Slack bot/user/app tokens used in earlier proof pastes must be rotated by the operator; agent cannot rotate workspace secrets.

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError`, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs stay `healthy` on connect.
- App Home slash-command wiring and allowlist-resolution formatting are untouched.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `main` `345083a5ab95` (single commit, parents=main).

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`, `action=block`), but the blocked result was returned as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper Rank-up on the previous abort-helper tip required the **canonical agent-core termination contracts** instead of `abortRun` at the embedded-run boundary (which records synthetic `stopReason: "aborted"` and can cancel sibling tools in mixed batches).

Dual-layer stop:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop blocked results → `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops single/all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `createAgentSession` → stops **mixed** batches when any finalized result has `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`.

Plugin / approval vetoes stay non-terminating.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the agent run instead of burning tokens indefinitely.
- Mixed parallel batches complete non-loop tools, then stop before the next provider turn.
- Non-loop blocks unchanged.
- Terminal outcome follows normal loop completion (not a synthetic aborted assistant message from embedded `abortRun`).

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `59977a726886274d04a036be59c7392972d67db9` (rebuilt from current `main`; replaces prior `critical-tool-loop-abort` approach)

**Patch quality:** platinum-shaped — 6 files, +232/−1 net, single owner boundary, no speculative exports, clean compare vs main.

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Replace embedded abort with terminate + post-turn contracts | done |
| Cover single-tool + mixed-batch | done (`agent-loop.test.ts`, `blocked-result.test.ts`) |
| e2e asserts `terminate: true` on tool-loop blocks | done |
| Real-runtime transcript (no next provider turn; no unintended aborted entry) | **pending L3** — need live agent credentials/run |

### Commands (green locally)

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <touched 6 files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "critical|shouldStopAfterTurn|mixed batch"

✓ Agent.prompt single critical terminate
Tests  2 passed | 25 skipped

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
Test Files  2 shards passed (4 + 27)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts -t "loop detection"

Tests  38 passed | 45 skipped
```

### Before / after (contract)

|---|---|---|
| Critical tool-loop block (single tool) | result returned; model continues | `terminate: true` → batch terminates; no next provider turn |
| Critical tool-loop in mixed batch | continue if not every result terminates | `shouldStopAfterTurn` stops after turn |
| Other blocked reasons | unchanged | unchanged (no `terminate`) |

Fixes #106231

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` passes `maxOptions: 20` explicitly to `normalizePollInput`
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, reject 21)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and `buildPollStartContent(..., { maxOptions: 20 })`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now enforced at the Matrix boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Vitest unit tests for Matrix poll types, Matrix outbound adapter, and shared poll helper contract.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/polls.test.ts
  pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # src/polls.test.ts — 7 passed
  - "does not limit options when maxOptions is omitted" → 50 options accepted ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 11 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "rejects more than 20 poll options per MSC3381" → throws "at most 20" ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts — 6 passed
  - "declares a 20-option poll maximum..." → outbound.pollMaxOptions = 20 ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary. Public helper contract preserved (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 rejected (protocol boundary in `buildPollStartContent`)
  - Matrix outbound: `pollMaxOptions = 20` declared on static adapter
  - Public helper: omitted `maxOptions` does not limit (contract preserved)

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Matrix outbound adapter did not declare `pollMaxOptions`, unlike all other poll channel adapters (Discord, WhatsApp, MS Teams, Telegram).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No Matrix-owned poll option limit enforcement.

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

**Real environment tested:** Linux WSL2, Node `v22.22.0`, local checkout of this branch.

### Path-level proof (production `ReefTransportClient` + negative control)

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-reef-relay-json-bound.ts
success overflow cancelled=true emittedBytes=16908288 error=reef.relay: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
error overflow name=ReefRelayError status=503 message=relay HTTP 503 cancelled=true emittedBytes=81920
negative control response.json() cancelled=false emittedBytes=262144
ok
```

Interpretation:

- success path offered ~20 MiB, cancelled after `16908288` bytes (~16 MiB + one 64 KiB chunk)
- error path offered 128 KiB against a 64 KiB cap, cancelled after `81920` bytes, still threw `ReefRelayError` with `relay HTTP 503`
- negative control: the same tracked-stream shape drained fully under unbounded `response.json()` with `cancelled=false`

### Focused Vitest regression

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `2de7b8c91e1ed785a490369117ad51915e6ea6d2`

### Executable negative control + wrap proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts -- --run -t "chunk-idle|negative" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=53 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000

      Tests  5 passed | 11 skipped (16)
```

## Real behavior proof

Production `downloadInboundMedia` → real `saveMediaStream` (no media-store mock) with a stalled Baileys AsyncIterable.


- **Boundary:** real media store write path; only Baileys download is stubbed to return a never-yielding stream.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` readdirSync flake and OpenClawKit dead-code job are unrelated to this surface.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe) and prove stalled-handshake exit + `initialize` failure with a short test-only hang floor.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Codex app-server endpoint that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin `initialize`/RPC forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` → transport `exit` / client error), so the run can stop or recover instead of hanging.

## Evidence

Head: `a02be68e1107857c4808cc9e93e1af5b10c7f1f1`

### Wiring + hang regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=30000
```

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph. This PR fixes that by using `Intl.Segmenter` to properly extract grapheme clusters.

## Summary

- **Problem**: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit), breaking on emoji/astral Unicode.
- **Solution**: New `deriveAvatarInitial` helper using `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` for complete grapheme clusters. Falls back to surrogate pair-aware extraction for browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` (Firefox 114-124).
- **What changed**: 
  - `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` with feature detection and fallback
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback
- **What did NOT change**: ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites (ASCII-only inputs).

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware)

## Evidence

**Environment**: jsdom with real Lit component rendering + Playwright E2E tests

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Unit tests
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts

# Playwright E2E tests
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
Unit tests (22 passed):
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter:
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" (complete family emoji)
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸" (complete flag)
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻" (skin tone preserved)
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (simple emoji)

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124 fallback):
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render: Real Lit component renders grapheme correctly

Playwright E2E tests (45 passed):
✓ ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts — 44 passed
  - Full Control UI with mocked Gateway WebSocket in real Chromium
  - Routing, app boot, Gateway handshake, and visible UI behavior verified
```

**What was not tested**: Live browser screenshots (jsdom + Playwright provides sufficient coverage)

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage: Unit test + Component test + E2E
- Target files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji, joined emoji, flags, skin-tone, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path
  - Selector: grapheme preserved in real Lit component DOM

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

## Evidence

Head: `4d348f869a9b7395123a205cc2545e1f1a3c0ea2`

### Unit + executable negative control

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[zalo proxyCache negative control] unbounded_size=65 unbounded_keeps_oldest=true bounded_size=64 bounded_evicts_oldest=true
[zalo proxyCache proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Real behavior proof (production path)

No `makeProxyFetch` mock. Calls production `resolveZaloProxyFetch` → SDK `makeProxyFetch` (Undici `ProxyAgent` wrappers) against 65 distinct loopback proxy URLs.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[zalo proxyCache production proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true real_makeProxyFetch=true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- **Boundary crossed:** process-local Undici ProxyAgent-backed fetch wrappers (real `makeProxyFetch`), no fetch-runtime mock.
- **Negative control:** plain Map without `pruneMapToMaxSize` retains oldest after 65 inserts; production path rebuilds oldest after the 64-entry cap.
- **Siblings:** Nextcloud Talk / MS Teams / Mattermost `pruneMapToMaxSize` callers unchanged.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` fail on `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` (`readdirSync: 54`) is tooling flake unrelated to this Zalo surface.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
```
